Build prompt

Rebuild this animation 1:1: Mileways' pricing screen - an auto-playing horizontal carousel of feature screenshots synced to feature labels, above the subscription tier toggle and trial button.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
A light paywall: "Unlock every detail about your flights." headline with an App Store rating line, then a carousel of phone-screenshot feature cards (Live Activities, Real-time Flight Alerts, and more), each captioned below. At the bottom: a "Real-time alerts" toggle row, a Yearly (with monthly-equivalent price) / Weekly tier selector, and a dark "Start your 7 day trial" button.

## Motion spec
Pattern: auto-advancing synced carousel.
- The carousel auto-plays: every 3s the current card slides left and the next enters from the right (300ms, ease-out) with a slight scale settle (0.96 to 1); the outgoing card dims as it exits.
- Peeking edges: the previous and next cards show ~24px slivers at the screen edges throughout.
- The caption below crossfades in sync (200ms, offset 50ms after the card starts moving) - title and subtitle swap together.
- Manual swipe overrides auto-play: the carousel tracks the finger 1:1 with rubber-banding at the ends, snaps to the nearest card (spring ~380/24), and the auto-play timer restarts after 4s idle.
- The tier selector slides a pill highlight between Yearly and Weekly (200ms spring) and the price text counts/crossfades to the new value.
- The trial button idles with a barely-there shimmer sweep across its surface every 6s.

## Calibration
- Auto-play must pause while the user touches the carousel and resume only after idle.
- Caption and card never desync: the caption belongs to the centered card at all times, even mid-swipe (crossfade at the 50% point).

## Reduced motion
Static first card; carousel advances only on manual swipe with instant caption swaps.

## Don't miss
- The page's only dark element is the trial button - everything else sits on white.
- The yearly price is shown as its per-month equivalent with the billing note beneath; don't merge them into one line.
